transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brought me in is that some nights after work, or if dinner’s been tense, I start eating and it’s like… the decision-making part of me just shuts off. I can kind of see myself reaching for more food, like I’m watching it happen, but I can’t make myself stop. It sounds strange saying it out loud.

Work’s been odd lately too—customers get so impatient over little things, like coupons not scanning—and I come home already wound up, and then if the evening goes badly, it just sort of… happens.
After these episodes of eating where you feel like you can’t stop, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Yeah… I mean, not every time, but there have been times. Usually after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I’ll take laxatives. I tell myself it’s just to… undo the damage, I guess.

It’s embarrassing to say. I’m usually kind of shaky afterward, and then I feel stupid for doing it. Like, I’ll notice the toothpaste on the sink or think about how the downstairs bathroom fan makes that rattling noise, and I’m standing there acting like that’s the problem, not what I just did.
How often do these episodes of feeling unable to stop eating happen—like, how many times a week or month?

Um… I’d say for the last few months it’s been most weeks. Like, usually there’s at least one night where I get that out-of-control feeling with food.

It’s not like I mark it on a calendar or anything—I probably should, I guess, the way I do with my work shifts on the fridge—but yeah, most weeks there’s one of those nights. And then afterward I’ll try to make up for it somehow, like throwing up, or taking laxatives, or sometimes skipping meals the next day, or forcing myself to go on a really long walk even if I’m tired.
When you're eating during these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what you're eating?

Yeah… that’s probably the clearest way to put it. It feels like I’m not really choosing anymore. I’ll start eating after work or after a tense dinner, and then it’s like the part of me that decides “okay, stop now” just goes quiet.

I can see myself getting more food—like, I know what I’m doing—but I can’t seem to interrupt it. It’s weird, because at work I can follow a register screen and count change and deal with people asking about coupons, but then at home in those moments I can’t manage something as basic as putting the food away.
During these episodes, do you ever feel completely unable to control how much you eat, like you're just going through the motions and can't break the cycle, even though you want to?

Yeah… that’s kind of the thing that made me come in, honestly. Some nights after work, or if dinner’s tense, I start eating and it’s like the decision-making part of me just shuts off.

I can see myself reaching for more food—like I’m aware of it—but I can’t seem to make myself stop. It’s like I’m just going through the motions, even though part of me is thinking, “Why are you still doing this?”
Do these episodes of eating and trying to compensate for them cause you a lot of distress, or make it hard for you to function at work or home?

Yeah, it does bother me a lot. I mean, I’m still going to work—I’m not calling out or anything. I can get through my cashier shifts, scan things, be polite enough, do what I’m supposed to do.

But afterward, or at home, it kind of hangs over me. Like I’ll avoid sitting down for a family meal because I’m already worried about what I ate earlier, or what I’m going to do to make up for it. And sometimes I’m there but not really there, just distracted and doing the math in my head instead of listening.

It’s not like my whole life has fallen apart, but it’s definitely starting to mess with how I am at home.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you've completely lost control over your actions, almost like you're on autopilot and can't make a different choice even though you want to?

Yeah… I think that’s what scares me about it. It’s not like I black out or anything—I know I’m there, I know I’m opening the cabinet or going back for more—but it feels like the part of me that’s supposed to make a different choice just sort of… shuts down.

It’s usually after work, or if dinner has been tense. And I’ll start eating, and then I can see myself reaching for more, almost like I’m watching it happen, but I can’t get myself to stop. Like at the register, I can make decisions all day—prices, coupons, people arguing over receipts—but in that moment at home, I can’t seem to do the one thing I’m telling myself to do.
Are there times when you start eating even when you’re not feeling upset or stressed, and you still feel like you can’t stop once you begin?

I mean… usually it’s tied to something, like after work or if dinner gets tense at home. That’s when it starts most often.

But once I start, that’s the part that feels the same regardless—I can see myself going back for more food, opening things, grabbing another bite, and it’s like I can’t get the decision-making part of my brain to kick back in. Like I’m aware of it happening, but I can’t make myself stop.

Sorry, I know you asked if it happens when I’m not upset… I guess I’m not totally sure. I focus more on the nights where I come home wound up, because those are the ones that stick out.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than you normally would, like you're rushing through the food without really thinking about it?

I don’t know if I’d say “much more quickly,” exactly. I haven’t really timed it or anything. I mean, sometimes I’m standing in the kitchen and eating instead of sitting down, so maybe it looks rushed, but I’m not sure that’s the main thing I notice.

It’s funny, at work I’m always thinking about speed—like how fast the line is moving, whether someone behind me is annoyed, whether the card reader is going to freeze again. So when I get home I’m not really paying attention to speed in the same way. I’m more just… in it, I guess.

So, yeah, I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed that part clearly.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

I… I’m not sure if that’s the reason. I mean, I am usually by myself when it happens, but that’s also just how the house kind of is at certain times, you know? Like after a shift, I get home and everyone’s doing their own thing, or the kitchen’s quiet.

Embarrassed… maybe? I don’t know. I don’t really think it through in the moment like, “I need to hide this.” It’s more that I don’t want to have to explain myself, I guess. But I’m not sure I’ve really noticed it as the main reason.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full, even if you know you’ve already had enough?

I guess the “full” part isn’t always what I’m paying attention to. Sometimes I do realize I’ve already had enough, but the thing that scares me is more that I can see myself still reaching for more food anyway.

Like after work, especially if I come home all keyed up, or if dinner was tense, I’ll start eating and it’s like the part of me that’s supposed to make the decision just… shuts off. I know that sounds dramatic. It’s not like I black out or anything. I’m watching myself open something else or go back for another bite, and I’m thinking, “Okay, stop,” but I don’t actually stop.

So, uncomfortably full… maybe sometimes, but what brought me in was more that I can’t seem to make myself stop once it starts.
